title: Could AI Change the Price You Pay at the Store?
summary:
Imagine you and a friend buy the exact same groceries from the same store, but your bill comes out higher. That is the worry behind a new look at how companies use artificial intelligence to set prices.

In one test, 400 shoppers bought the same 20 items from the same stores on Instacart. The prices were not the same. For some items, the difference was as much as 23 percent.

Lindsay Owens leads a consumer group called Groundwork Collaborative. She worked with researchers to study the test. Soon after the test became public, Instacart stopped it. The company said the tests raised concerns.

Owens says many companies are comfortable changing prices. Computer programs called algorithms can shift prices based on personal data.

Owens and Elizabeth Pancotti also studied 315 patents. They found Walmart patent ideas for technology that could link to a smartwatch. But Walmart executive Dan Bartlett said the company will not use a customer's personal information to set a price just for that person. The question now is how companies choose to use it.
why_it_matters: The price you pay for snacks or groceries could change depending on who you are, so it matters to know how prices are set.

keywords.explanation: Artificial intelligence is computer smarts that let machines learn and make choices like people do.
Algorithms are sets of rules a computer follows to make a choice or solve a problem.
Patents are papers that give an inventor the right to be the one who uses a new idea.
A smartwatch is a watch you wear on your wrist that can run apps and track things about you.
A consumer is a person who buys and uses things like food and clothes.

questions.question: What did the test of shoppers buying the same groceries show?
options: Only one shopper could buy the items
The prices were not the same for everyone
Everyone paid exactly the same price
questions.correct_answer: The prices were not the same for everyone

Who leads the consumer group Groundwork Collaborative?
What did Instacart do soon after the test became public?
options: It shared the test with more stores

options: Use a customer's personal information to set a price just for that person
questions.correct_answer: Use a customer's personal information to set a price just for that person

background_read: Some stores use computer programs to help decide what things cost.
These programs can look at personal data and change prices for different shoppers.
That is why people are asking whether the same item should cost the same for everyone.
Article_Structure: WHO: Lindsay Owens, researchers, Elizabeth Pancotti, Instacart, Walmart executive Dan Bartlett, and shoppers.
WHAT: A study found that the same groceries bought from the same stores could cost different amounts for different shoppers.
WHERE: On Instacart, at the same stores where shoppers bought the same 20 items.
WHY: Companies use artificial intelligence and algorithms that can shift prices based on personal data.

Instacart said the tests raised concerns.
